defects.before: The program uses the name only as a column title of the C rows.
defects.after: The interval mode uses the name in two places: as a column title in the header line of the C rows (line 3031), and in the error message of `open_counters` (line 1598).
defects.evidence: grep of `ev_name` in bwx12.c shows a use at line 1598 (the stderr message of open_counters) besides line 3031, and three more uses in the trial mode (lines 2130, 2477, 2518).

defects.before: So before every timed interval the thread has read its whole buffer once with the same kernel.
defects.after: So before every timed interval the thread has run the same kernel once over its whole buffer.
defects.evidence: For `read_1pl` the warm-up call loads only 16 B of each 64 B line (source lines 994 to 997, listing.txt lines 757 to 760), so the thread has not read the whole buffer.

defects.before: (4 bullets; the last one ends with) So this output can run while the workers do their warm-up.
defects.after: (added 5th bullet) The output ends before the next timed interval starts. The barrier of line 1675 lets the workers pass only when `main` has finished the output and waits at line 3057.
defects.evidence: main prints the P rows and flushes at lines 3115 to 3120 before it calls pthread_barrier_wait at line 3057, and the barrier needs all 121 threads (line 3005), so no output of main can lie inside a timed interval.

defects.before: In the test `t0` is 2 us to 34 us after the common start time (us = microsecond, computed on 2026-11-21 from the columns `t_sched_s` and `t_start_s` of all 8880 T rows) [Ref5].
defects.after: (same sentence, then added) Both columns are printed with 6 decimal places, so each time is rounded to 1 us.
defects.evidence: Line 3081 prints the times with `%.6f` seconds; my recomputation over the 9 csv files gave 2 us and 34 us, each a difference of two values rounded to 1 us.

defects.before: **Common start, step 1.** The thread spins until the shared counter `gen` equals `k + 1`. ... The loop body is empty, so the thread stays on its CPU and does not sleep.
defects.after: **Common start, step 1.** Lines 1676 to 1683 run only with `--stop common`, which the test uses. The thread repeats an empty loop until the shared counter `gen` equals `k + 1`. ... In this loop the thread stays on its CPU and does not sleep.
defects.evidence: Line 1676 is `if (cfg.stop_common)`, a condition that the row did not explain; the verb "spins" was replaced by the literal description of the empty loop of lines 1677 to 1678.

defects.before: So the thread walks its 256 MiB buffer from start to end, again and again, until the interval ends.
defects.after: So the kernel calls go through the 256 MiB buffer from start to end and then start again at byte 0, until the interval ends.
defects.evidence: "walks" is a metaphor; lines 1697 to 1699 add the chunk size to `at` and set it to 0 when it equals `size`.

defects.before: `main` calls it for an unknown option and for settings that do not fit together.
defects.after: `main` calls it for an argument that it does not accept and for settings that fail one of its checks (lines 2969 to 2995), for example `--threads` without `--cpus`.
defects.evidence: grep of `usage()` shows calls at lines 2954, 2959 and 2966 (bad word after --stop or --start, unknown option) and at lines 2971, 2974, 2985 and 2994 (failed checks, which include a missing --seq, so "do not fit together" was both a metaphor and too narrow).

defects.before: **Late flag.** It is set when `t0` is more than 100000 ns (100 us, `LATE_NS`) after the common start time. `main` then prints `late` in the last column of the T row. In the test no T row has the flag [Ref5].
defects.after: **Late flag.** It is set when `t0` is more than 100000 ns (100 us, `LATE_NS`) after the common start time. `main` then prints `late` in the last column of the T row. The program does nothing else with the flag: the interval runs, and its bytes are counted. In the test no T row has the flag [Ref5].
defects.evidence: grep of bwx12.c shows the field `late` only at line 1725 (set) and line 3084 (printed), so this check stops nothing, and the row did not say so.

defects.before: - In the test the last `t1` is 0 us to 463 us after the deadline, and the elapsed time `t1 - t0` is 5.999979 s to 6.000457 s (computed on 2026-11-21 from all 8880 T rows) [Ref5].
defects.after: - In the test the last `t1` is 0 us to 463 us after the deadline [Ref5]. The elapsed time `t1 - t0` is 5.999979 s to 6.000457 s. Both ranges were computed on 2026-11-21 from all 8880 T rows, with the deadline taken as `t_sched_s` plus 6 s.
defects.evidence: One 36-word sentence carried two claims, and the deadline is not a column of the T row; my recomputation over the 8880 T rows of the 9 csv files gives 0 to 463 us for t_end_s - (t_sched_s + 6) and 5.999979 to 6.000457 s for elapsed_s.
